answer: Sybil resistance via vouching bonds: each agent is a vertex in a trust graph, and a newcomer joins the trusted core only when established peers vouch for it by staking a bond that is slashed if it later cheats. 1,000 spun-up sybils just form an isolated island with zero edges into the core and zero economic weight. To break in, an attacker must bribe real vouchers, each risking a 100 POA bond, so 1,000 fakes put 100,000 POA at slashing risk. The voyage from fresh vertex to trusted earner costs real capital, not cheap copies.
